title: Apply F = G m1 m2 / r^2

hook.scenario: ISRO ko satellite launch karte waqt pata hona chahiye ki Earth satellite ko kitni force se kheeche gi har height par — warna satellite ya toh crash kar jaayega ya space mein kho jaayega.
hook.question: Agar tumhe kisi planet ke surface par gravitational force nikaalini ho, toh kaise karoge?

mental_model.intuition: F = G m₁ m₂ / r² ek calculator hai — masses aur distance daalo, gravitational force nikal jaayegi.
mental_model.description: Socho jaise ek bill calculate karte ho: items ki cost multiply karo, phir kuch divide karo. Yahaan bhi masses multiply karo, r² se divide karo, aur G se scale karo. Bas powers of 10 carefully handle karna — yahi main skill hai.

explanation:
Ab tumne law padh liya, toh ab usse problems mein apply karna seekho. Sabse pehle samjho ki formula mein kya kya daalna hai: m₁ aur m₂ dono objects ke masses (kg mein), r dono ke CENTRES ke beech ki distance (metres mein) — surface se surface nahi.

Sabse common mistake yeh hai ki jab object Earth ke surface par ho, toh r = Earth ka RADIUS (6.4 × 10⁶ m) hota hai, kyunki distance centre se measure hoti hai. Agar object h height par ho, toh r = R + h.

Powers of 10 handle karna yahan sabse important skill hai. Tip: pehle coefficients multiply/divide karo alag se, phir powers of 10 alag se. Jaise: (6.674 × 10⁻¹¹) × (6 × 10²⁴) = (6.674 × 6) × 10⁻¹¹⁺²⁴ = 40.04 × 10¹³.

Kuch important variations jo boards mein aate hain: (a) Agar ek mass double ho jaaye toh force double ho jaayegi. (b) Agar distance half ho jaaye toh force 4 guna ho jaayegi. (c) Agar dono masses triple ho jaayein aur distance bhi triple, toh force same rahegi (9/9 = 1). In sab mein formula mein directly substitute karke ratio nikaal lo.

Ek aur important application: g derive karna. Earth ke surface par kisi object (mass m) par gravitational force = mg. Isko F = G M m / R² se equate karo: mg = G M m / R², cancel m, toh g = G M / R². Isliye g alag planets par alag hota hai — M aur R alag hain.

key_points.title: Distance r is centre-to-centre
key_points.detail: On Earth's surface, r = R (radius of Earth, 6.4 × 10⁶ m), NOT zero.

key_points.title: Powers of 10 trick
key_points.detail: Handle coefficients and powers separately: multiply/divide coefficients, then add/subtract exponents.

key_points.title: Deriving g
key_points.detail: g = G M / R². This connects the universal law to free-fall acceleration.

key_points.title: Proportionality shortcuts
key_points.detail: F ∝ m₁m₂ and F ∝ 1/r². Use ratios for 'what happens if...' questions without calculating.

worked_example.problem: Calculate the force of gravity on a 50 kg person standing on Earth's surface. (M = 6 × 10²⁴ kg, R = 6.4 × 10⁶ m, G = 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻²)

steps.narration: Values note karo — person Earth ke surface par hai toh r = R (Earth ka radius).
steps.math: m₁ = 6 × 10²⁴ kg, m₂ = 50 kg, r = 6.4 × 10⁶ m

worked_example.answer: F ≈ 490 N. Cross-check: mg = 50 × 9.8 = 490 N ✓ — formula gives exactly the weight!

worked_example.problem: Two spheres of masses 20 kg and 30 kg are placed with their centres 0.5 m apart. Find the gravitational force between them.

steps.narration: Chhote objects hain, toh force bahut chhoti hogi — but calculate karte hain.
steps.math: m₁ = 20 kg, m₂ = 30 kg, r = 0.5 m

worked_example.answer: F ≈ 1.6 × 10⁻⁷ N — itni chhoti force ki feel bhi nahi hogi, tabhi daily life mein objects ek doosre ki taraf nahi khisakte.

common_mistakes.title: r mein Earth ka radius bhoolna
common_mistakes.explanation: Jab object Earth ke surface par hai, toh r = 0 nahi hai! r = Earth ka radius (6.4 × 10⁶ m) hai, kyunki distance centre-to-centre hoti hai.

common_mistakes.title: Powers of 10 mein galti
common_mistakes.explanation: 10⁻¹¹ × 10²⁴ = 10¹³, nahi ki 10⁻²⁶⁴. Exponents ADD hote hain multiplication mein. Isko carefully likho step by step.

common_mistakes.title: Units miss karna
common_mistakes.explanation: Force ka answer N (Newton) mein hona chahiye. Agar masses kg mein aur distance m mein nahi daali, toh answer galat aayega.

recall_questions.q: What is r in the formula F = G m₁ m₂ / r² when an object is on Earth's surface?
recall_questions.answer: r = R, the radius of the Earth (approximately 6.4 × 10⁶ m), because r is the distance between the centres of the two objects.

recall_questions.q: Derive the expression for acceleration due to gravity g from the universal law.
recall_questions.answer: For a body of mass m on Earth's surface: mg = G M m / R². Cancel m: g = G M / R².

recall_questions.q: If both masses and the distance are tripled, what happens to the gravitational force?
recall_questions.answer: F' = G(3m₁)(3m₂)/(3r)² = 9Gm₁m₂/9r² = F. The force remains unchanged.

oa_questions.question: Calculate the force of gravitation between the Earth and the Sun, given that the mass of the Earth = 6 × 10²⁴ kg and of the Sun = 2 × 10³⁰ kg. The average distance between the two is 1.5 × 10¹¹ m.
oa_questions.approach: Substitute values into F = Gm₁m₂/r², handle exponents carefully.

oa_questions.question: How does the force of gravitation between two objects change when the distance between them is reduced to half?
oa_questions.answer: F' = G m₁ m₂ / (r/2)² = G m₁ m₂ / (r²/4) = 4 × G m₁ m₂ / r² = 4F. The force becomes four times.
oa_questions.approach: Substitute r/2 for r in the formula and simplify the ratio F'/F.
